# Source: CHANGELOG.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/CHANGELOG.html

## [1.11.26] - 2026-11-27

### Changed
- Version housekeeping, no cell version changes. Nucleus and Receptor lockfiles state their package versions; Cytosol, Mitosis, Ribosome and Genome changelogs drop `[Unreleased]` blocks that had already shipped; Membrane, Nucleus and Receptor changelogs are ordered by version; the Membrane, Genome and Ribosome tool documents match the catalog; the runtime README names 1.4.5. Phenotype pins the zod advisory fix in its Remotion test fixture.

## [1.11.25] - 2026-11-26

### Security
- `hela-runtime` 1.4.5: one permission gate covers retrieval, planning and dispatch in `hela.agent.run`; write-banned and lookup-only tasks get read-only tools, banned page actions are refused, and paths or filenames no longer pull destructive tools into the shortlist (hela-runtime#9). Ban detection understands English only; other limits are listed in the runtime changelog.

### Fixed
- Namespaced catalogs plan and execute, and the model's tool picks no longer depend on the naming mode (hela-runtime#8). A time question opens with the clock tool (hela-runtime#4). Catalog search matches cell names.

## [1.11.24] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed
- `hela-runtime` 1.4.4: `hela.agent.run` no longer ends "single action complete" after one non-failing call to a tool that does not address the task; unanswered runs end `degraded` (hela-runtime#4, RT-07). A write ban scoped to the task's own input keeps a permitted copy (RT-03), a timed-out read is retried once (RT-04), a plan cut short by `maxToolCalls` is `degraded` with `pendingSteps` (RT-05) and early exits return `status: "failed"` (RT-06). A ban naming a concrete file or path stays a full write ban.

## [1.11.23] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed
- `hela-runtime` 1.4.3 gives the Mitosis cell `HELA_RUNTIME_URL`: a loopback-only endpoint on an ephemeral port behind a random capability path, so cross-cell workflow steps no longer fail with `No runtime transport bound`. An operator-set value still wins (chaining-mcp#28, ISS-61).
- `hela-mitosis` 3.1.3: the three LLM planners share the model-backed time budget instead of the 10 s cap, `get_skill` distinguishes unknown skill, file not in skill and path not allowed, `maxChars` counts the body, `search_prompts` reports an empty category match, and prompt `expectedTools` use real tool names (ISS-62, ISS-63).
- `hela-ribosome` 3.2.4: a server from `opencode_server_spawn` keeps its generated password inside the cell and passes it to attached agents, a startup failure is reported, `opencode_import` is `ok:false` when nothing imported and takes `cwd`, and follow-up runs get unique names (menager-mcp#23, ISS-64…66).
- `hela-genome` 3.3.0: tombstones carry `deleted_at` and report their age, `restore:true` re-creates a deleted name, a stale edited copy cannot resurrect a deleted entity, `delete_entities` reaches central-only entities, `read_graph` pages stop at about 100 KB with `truncated` and `nextCursor`, and the year-32971 repair is an explicit `repair_timestamps` action (project-mcp#41, ISS-67, 68, 70, 71).
- `hela-enzyme` 4.3.4: `news_monitor` and the `google_search` news fallback mark publisher-home links, `fact_checker` judges each source against the claim (supports, refutes or unclear), and CSV export keeps plain numbers unquoted and includes columns that only later rows have (researcher-mcp#44, ISS-72…74; the alphabetical column order did not reproduce in the cell).

## [1.11.22] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.8 repairs the cookie handling reopened in browser-mcp#22. `browser_save_session` keeps real cookie values in its owner-only, page-scoped file, so `browser_load_session` no longer overwrites a live cookie with the text `[redacted]`; masked cookies from older saves are skipped and counted.
- `browser_upload` refuses credential and system paths (`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.config`, every `.env*`, `/etc`, …) by real path even when `HELA_ALLOWED_ROOTS` is `/` or `$HOME`; `HELA_BROWSER_UPLOAD_ANY=true` still overrides.
- `browser_export_state` and `browser_save_session` write 0600 atomically (temp file + rename), replacing an existing world-readable file instead of chmod'ing it by path.
- Cytosol pin moved to the merge commit `93681e7`; `latest-stable` and the `v1.11.22` snapshot pair carry it.

## [1.11.21] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed
- `hela-runtime` 1.4.2 stops reporting a clean success when the tool it called failed. Failed payloads and thrown errors are recorded as failed, an identical failing call is skipped instead of retried verbatim, and the result carries `ok`, `status`, `failedCalls`, `degraded` and `decision.action: "failed"` (hela-runtime#4).
- A task that forbids modification is enforced on the final tool selection: "Read notes.txt. Do not edit any files." executes `read_file` instead of writing, and a run with no permitted tool stops with `no permitted tools` (hela-runtime#5, RT-01).
- `classifyToolResult` honours `isError` on results that carry `structuredContent` but no `content` array and reads failure/degradation from `structuredContent` first, so `hela.pipe` is fail-closed again for that shape. The classifier is shared by the pipe and the native agent (hela-runtime#5, RT-02; hela-mcp-ecosystem#8).
- Runtime pin and `latest-stable` snapshot now point at the 1.4.2 merge commit; the runtime suite is 74/74.

## [1.11.20] - 2026-11-24

### Fixed
- `doctor.mjs --hosts` no longer counts the runtime's aggregate tool entry on top of the cells. A `HELA_NAMESPACE_TOOLS=0` host showed "287 declared tools shadowed by bare-name collisions" and recommended enabling namespacing, when the real gap was zero: 593 declared was 295 cell tools plus the runtime's 298 already-aggregated names. The check now compares live tools against the cells only and reports 9 ok, 0 warn on lappy.

## [1.11.19] - 2026-11-24

### Fixed
- The apply result now uses the same profile-aware comparison as the check. 1.11.18 filtered snapshot additions in the check and the pre-apply decision but left the post-apply summary comparing the whole snapshot, so a `dev-workspace` update still printed `hela-receptor` and `hela-plastid` as added. All four `compareRelease` call sites now pass the profile's cell set.

## [1.11.18] - 2026-11-24

### Fixed
- The update controller no longer reports a permanent update for profile installations. `compareRelease` compared every snapshot cell against the installed profile subset, so a `dev-workspace` install treated `hela-receptor` and `hela-plastid` as "added" on every check and kept `update-available` true even at the latest snapshot. It now filters snapshot additions to the profile's own cells; removals are still reported. (`scripts/update-controller.mjs`, one regression test)

## [1.11.17] - 2026-11-24

### Fixed
- `hela-phenotype` 3.3.0 returns every Ellis UI page (index, letter, note, slideshow) and accepts a `page` selector, so the links inside the returned templates resolve. The list tool is a compact JSON index instead of 24 full design documents, both tools emit real newlines instead of literal `\n`, and the false "Zero Dependencies" claim now states the actual Tailwind CDN, Google Fonts and icon dependencies. (`designer-mcp#41`)

## [1.11.16] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-enzyme` 4.3.3: summarizer drops page chrome, dedup returns survivors with URL canonicalisation, fact_checker reports stances and a verdict, research_assistant dedups across queries, wikipedia loses the empty parentheses, and multi_site_search reports per-site counts.

## [1.11.15] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.7 marks mock-served requests so synthetic traffic is distinguishable from real traffic, with filters and an exposed mock count.

## [1.11.14] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-ribosome` 3.2.3: the trigger-echo strip no longer lets a bare newline consume the pending echo, removing a race that flaked the hook regression under CI.

## [1.11.13] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-ribosome` 3.2.2: `session_read` lines mode replays carriage-return redraws, removing interleaved prompt echoes.
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.6: `extract_schema` reads JSON-LD/microdata/tables, `emulate` sets language and Accept-Language, `get_state` exposes checked/name/textBlocks, captcha verify is honest, and intercept/switch_tab/cache are diagnosed.
- `hela-mitosis` 3.1.2: prompt `expectedTools` map to real HeLa tools with a catalog test, the category enum is derived from data, the local instruction fallback is marked degraded, and `execute:false` records a proposed call.

## [1.11.12] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-phenotype` 3.2.3 removes the local `docs/TOOLS.md` generator that 3.2.2 added; the file stays owned by `npm run docs:generate -- --servers`. The consistency test keeps its live `tools/list` count checks.

## [1.11.11] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- Tool references in phenotype, cytosol, genome, enzyme, mitosis and ribosome are regenerated from the schema catalog. Several had drifted (missing tools, stale descriptions) because the file is not regenerated by the cell release, only by `npm run docs:generate -- --servers`.

## [1.11.10] - 2026-11-23

### Fixed
- `hela-phenotype` 3.2.2 publishes only derived numbers: 37 slop gates, 68 brands in 9 categories, 14 motion categories, 19 themes, 18 systems, and the tool count from `tools/list`. Two rules that contradicted the code are removed, `get_reference` no longer leaks its absolute path, and a consistency test fails when a claim drifts.

## [1.11.9] - 2026-11-23

### Changed
- `hela-genome` 3.2.0 requires `HELA_GENOME_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true` for `insert_data`, `update_data` and `import_data`, matching `delete_data`; `read_graph` is paged with `nextCursor`. **Breaking for bulk writes.**

### Fixed
- Genome: AKIA keys detected with named finding types, one-commit repositories report modified and untracked files, the pre-commit hook cannot delete after a failed merge, `bug:` guidance matches `openBugs`, and empty conditions are rejected explicitly.

## [1.11.8] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.5 returns vision boxes with explicit units: `bbox` normalised 0-1, `bboxPx` in source pixels, `image` dimensions and `coordinateSpace`. The preprocessed OCR image moved to `imageBase64` so `image` means dimensions.

## [1.11.7] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.4 restores the restricted wording on `browser_search` that 3.3.3 dropped while documenting its tools scope; the canonical-boundary check asserts it.

## [1.11.6] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.3: `browser_switch_to_new_tab` no longer throws, quiz batches report real counts, macro export honours format and save, generated tests run, and catalogue search finds tool names.
- `hela-genome` 3.1.3: harness sync cannot store a fabricated year (zero and seconds timestamps are normalised or skipped with a reason, existing bogus rows repaired), `get_timeline` uses real timestamps with numeric `since` and sorts, and the dry run honours watermarks.

## [1.11.5] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- The Cytosol tool count in the site and `llms.txt` is derived from the generated catalog instead of a hand-written number, and the docs test compares against the catalog rather than the literal `75`. Adding `browser_list_dialogs` in cytosol 3.3.2 made the stale literal fail the gh-pages verification job.

## [1.11.4] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-genome` 3.1.2: mission transitions are guarded (queued → claimed → in_progress → completed/failed, cancel from any state, explicit requeue), lifecycle updates must name the claimant, and claims carry a 30-minute lease.
- `hela-enzyme` 4.3.2: citations keep every author, invert names per style, use et al. for MLA, and warn instead of dropping an unparseable name.
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.2: dialogs are dismissed by default instead of auto-accepted, `browser_dialog` sets the next action and prompt text, `browser_list_dialogs` records them, and popup dismissal never clicks an affirmative control.

## [1.11.3] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- Runtime 1.4.1 repinned at `14cc13e`: the version bump changed the npm deps derivation input, so the fixed-output `npmDepsHash` no longer matched and the Nix verify job failed. Hash refreshed (`sha256-VlP6gbWoi6TTkbk4FSSKey/bTw/rNT40H+99k7J4A7c=`); no functional change from 1.11.2.

## [1.11.2] - 2026-11-22

### Added
- **Response contract for degraded results.** `hela.runtime` 1.4.1 reports `status: ok | degraded | failed` on `hela.pipe`, per-step status, and a `degraded` array naming the step and reasons. A step that marks itself `degraded`, `partial`, `truncated`, `status: "degraded"` or `warnings` makes the pipe degraded while `ok` stays true. Contract documented in `hela-runtime/docs/response-contract.md`.
- `hela.mitosis` 3.1.1 adopts it: `get_skill` marks a truncated or file-omitted answer `status: "degraded"` with a reason.

### Fixed
- The nine instances tracked by #8 were fixed individually; this release makes the convention enforceable rather than per-tool.

## [1.11.1] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-genome` 3.1.1: entity deletions are reconciled across project and central sync, sync reports what it deleted or skipped, and a root switch no longer imports another project into a fresh root.
- `hela-enzyme` 4.3.1: sentiment applies negation across a window, so "never recommend" and "hardly a success" score negative; the negations found and the lexicon caveat are reported.
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.1: seventeen handlers expose their payload through `structuredContent` with a bounded text summary, and failures set `isError`.
- `hela-phenotype` 3.2.1: React components use their declared props and derive classes from the requested style and palette; the snippet is typechecked and rendered in tests.

## [1.11.0] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `hela-phenotype` 3.2.0: theme colours and every derived token are inside sRGB (0 of 342 emitted values out of gamut); `stitch_sync_design_system` writes one accent; browser templates apply their palette; the 8-state component renders 8 distinct states; logo search matches catalogue facets; the export covers `index.html`.
- `hela-enzyme` 4.3.0: trends report a window and never page counts as interest; CSV escapes quotes and guards formulas; research sessions persist to disk; `news_monitor` enforces `dateRestrict` and resolves redirects.
- `hela-mitosis` 3.1.0: `workflow_orchestrator` dispatches to named cells and marks failed steps failed; planners name a tool or say why not; analysis tools stop inventing metrics; skill frontmatter parses properly and the response is bounded.
- `hela-ribosome` 3.2.1: opencode v2 CLI alignment; follow-ups resume the addressed session; the managed-server password is redacted from session output; hooks wait for output rather than their own echo.
- `hela-cytosol` 3.3.0: cookies are page-scoped and redacted with explicit widening; uploads are contained to workspace roots; `browser_extract_table` honours `header` without eating a data row.
- `hela-genome` 3.1.0: deletes are durable across central sync; the secret scan no longer opens live SQLite files, so WAL locks and post-scan writes survive.

## [1.10.10] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `designer-mcp` 3.1.0: inline contrast is computed (WCAG 2.x) rather than string-matched, so white-on-white at 1.01:1 now fails and the sample page grades B/75 instead of A/96; palette variants pass achromatic inputs through unchanged; the High Contrast label names the surface it was measured against; derived `--color-focus` chroma is clamped into sRGB; and the five Stitch CLI tools are advertised only when the CLI is present (23 vs 28 tools, `HELA_PHENOTYPE_STITCH` overrides).

## [1.10.9] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- Repin the runtime to the commit that refreshes `npmDepsHash`. The 1.4.0 version bump changed the npm-deps derivation input, so the Nix verification job failed at build time on a fixed-output hash mismatch — the installer and CI both build from the pinned revision, which still carried the stale hash. No runtime behaviour change.

## [1.10.8] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `researcher-mcp` 4.2.2: the IDF half of the scorer was inert in production because `research_brief` passed no candidate corpus. Terms are now weighted by how much they discriminate among the returned pages, so a common term contributes little and a rare one carries the match.

## [1.10.7] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `researcher-mcp` 4.2.1: the enzyme fixes from 4.1.0/4.2.0 were compiled into a module the shipped entry never loads. The real `research_brief` (root `research-server.ts`) now backs off once on an empty ranked result, discloses it, returns the feedback handle, and appends spool signals from `extract_content`. Found by post-deploy verification: the pinned 4.2.0 cell still behaved like 4.0.9.

## [1.10.6] - 2026-11-22

### Changed
- **`hela.pipe` fails closed.** A chain whose middle step failed returned `ok: true` and piped the error text into the next step, which produced a confident result computed from `ENOENT`. `ok` now reflects every step, `failedStep` names the first failure, `onError` defaults to `stop`, and each result carries its own `ok`. This is a breaking default by intent: callers that checked `ok` were getting a wrong answer. Runtime 1.4.0.

## [1.10.5] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `filesystem-mcp` 3.0.6: four responses promised what the implementation did not deliver. Ranged `read_file` now snaps to character boundaries and reports `startByte`/`endByte` (chunked reads of non-ASCII files no longer lose a character per boundary); `extract_archive` reports `extracted`/`entries`/`skipped` with a reason instead of a silent partial success; `watch_file` buffers events and returns them on the next call (plus waits for chokidar's initial scan); `compare_files` reports `size` in bytes with a separate `characters` field and a correct line count.

## [1.10.4] - 2026-11-22

### Added
- The adaptive search priors can now learn. Enzyme observes when a caller follows up on a URL a brief returned and appends a used=true record (with display rank) to `~/.local/state/hela/search-feedback.jsonl`; genome drains that spool into `source_feedback` whenever `search_feedback` or `search_priors` is called. One writer keeps the table honest, the file is claimed by rename so nothing imports twice, and failed inserts are preserved for a retry. `hela-enzyme` 4.2.0, `hela-genome` 3.0.7.

## [1.10.3] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `chaining-mcp` 3.0.9: peer discovery reads the runtime's generated tool catalog, so Mitosis sees the ten cells it orchestrates when they are multiplexed behind one endpoint. `validate_tool_chain` no longer reports every real tool as unavailable (`read_file` on `hela-membrane` included), and availability now distinguishes an absent tool (error) from an undiscovered server or missing catalog (warning) — the direction that had been discarding correct plans. Verified against the installed catalog: 10 cells, 299 tools.

## [1.10.2] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- `terminal-mcp` 3.0.7: local commands run from a temporary script instead of `sh -c`, so `pkill -f` no longer matches and kills the wrapper shell, and `pgrep -f` no longer reports it as a live process. RTK summarisation rejects summaries below 5% of the source, retains and names the original output, and anchors its log heuristic to line starts. Two defects that both made a failed step look successful.
- `researcher-mcp` 4.1.0: `research_brief` retries once with a reduced query when every source returns nothing and discloses it (`backoff: "…"`); scoring folds morphological variants and weights terms by how much they discriminate among the candidates; the brief returns a feedback handle plus the exact `genome search_feedback` call, and a follow-up tool on a brief URL appends it with `used=true`.

## [1.10.1] - 2026-11-22

### Fixed
- Running `doctor` against a bare checkout printed ten rows of `missing*` / `Not checked` without naming a path or a next step, which is indistinguishable from a broken install — and reads as a platform bug when it happens on Windows. Rows now say `not installed`, and when every component is missing the report lists the paths it resolved plus the two commands that fix it (install, then `doctor --prefix`).
- A profile can be installed under any mode, but doctor only looked at `<profile>-individual` unless `--prefix` was passed. Installing with `--runtime` therefore made a healthy host report every component missing. When the default prefix has no manifest, doctor now scans for sibling `<profile>-*` installations and prints each one with the `--mode` or `--prefix` that would diagnose it; JSON output carries the same list under `installationCandidates`.

## [1.10.0] - 2026-11-21

### Added
- `doctor.mjs --hosts` inspects the layer the doctor previously ignored: the wiring between client applications and the runtime. It checks the interpreter floor derived from cell `engines`, whether `nodejs` is still marked manual for apt, the gate file the launcher reads, credential-file modes and key presence, all six client configs, backup exposure, and a live `initialize`/`tools/list` handshake. `--repair` reinstalls the pinned node package, re-asserts the manual mark and fixes credential/backup modes; exit codes remain 0/1/2.
- `scripts/host-entry.sh` is the canonical client entry point, installed as `~/.local/bin/hela-runtime-mcp`. It resolves the interpreter at spawn time, refuses to start below the required major, sources one 0600 credentials file, and logs failures because MCP hosts swallow child stderr. It is PATH-independent: every external command is absolute, so it reports a stripped environment instead of failing inside it.
- `docs/reliability.md` documents the host-to-cell failure model with eight diagrams. Sources are Mermaid under `assets/diagrams/`, renders are SVG beside them, because the document renderer carries `markdown-it` without Mermaid and escapes raw HTML.

### Changed
- Credentials found in client-config backups were copied into mema-vault before those backups were deleted, so the host doctor reports a clean backup surface instead of a permanent warning. `docs/reliability.md` documents vault-based recovery.

## [1.9.27] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- The Docker doctor reported `DEGRADED` with an empty `[]` on a clean image because it compared the runtime catalog against bare cell tool names. The container never receives `HELA_NAMESPACE_TOOLS`, so the runtime applies its new default and advertises `hela_membrane_read_file`; 23 of 24 expected names therefore looked missing. Coverage now accepts the runtime's namespaced name or the bare one, and a real gap names the cell and tool instead of printing an empty array. Unit tests cover both surfaces and a genuinely missing tool.
- Enzyme `4.0.9` runs its priors suite on Node 20 instead of failing at import: `node:sqlite` only exists from 22.5, so the database cases are gated on the runtime version while the resolution and collapse-guard tests still run. The package claims Node 20, where learned priors deliberately degrade to the static table.

## [1.9.26] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- Learned search priors never applied on a host whose genome still uses the legacy central store. Enzyme resolved `~/memory/memory.db` only, while genome keeps writing `~/memory.db` when its migration did not run — so every brief reported `priors: static` and the recorded decisions sat in a file nobody read. Enzyme now resolves the way genome does: the migrated path when it exists, otherwise the legacy file. Verified end to end with an isolated HOME: ten decisions land in the file the brief reads and it reports `priors: learned (10 samples)`.

## [1.9.25] - 2026-11-19

### Added
- The search loop closes through Genome. Genome `3.0.6` records which source produced the result a caller actually used in a `source_feedback` table in the central memory database, exposed as `search_feedback` (record) and `search_priors` (read). Enzyme `4.0.7` reads that table read-only with `node:sqlite` — no new dependency — and ranks `research_brief` / `multi_site_search` with the derived multipliers instead of constants, stating which table it used (`priors: static` or `priors: learned (N)`).
- The priors carry a collapse guard, because a feedback loop can starve itself: one unlucky run lowers a source's multiplier, the lower multiplier keeps its results under the relevance floor, no further samples arrive, and the mistake becomes permanent. A source with no samples in an active class, or whose newest sample is over 30 days old, is floored at 1.0 and lifted by 0.15 so it stays reachable. Three tests in each repo fail if the guard is removed.
- `scripts/check-prose-facts.mjs` now fails `docs:check` when hand-written prose restates a fact the build knows: an unknown Hela repository name, a live version literal, a roster claim that disagrees with the inventory or profile set, a licence no cell uses, or a per-profile server count that drifted. Ten tests prove each rule fires. It found two real drifts on its first run (a page claiming runtime 1.3.6 after the runtime moved, and a setup page pinning Phenotype 3.0.3 against an inventory at 3.0.5).

### Changed
- Runtime `1.3.7` namespaces cell tools by default: `hela_nucleus_execute_command` instead of `execute_command`. A bare name shadows whatever the host already exposes and the collision is settled by whichever server connected last. `HELA_NAMESPACE_TOOLS=0` restores the previous surface; this is breaking for clients that pin bare tool names, and the manifest cache key already covers the mode so a switching client rebuilds its fingerprints once.
- Genome creates the parent directory of a configured database path. `GUARDIAN_CENTRAL_DB` pointing into a directory that did not exist yet used to die with `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` on the first query.

### Closed
- Four Dependabot pull requests (chaining `#13`, `#18`; filesystem `#17`, `#16`) were closed as already satisfied: both default branches resolve zod 4.6.7, glob 14.0.6 and minimatch 11.0.9.
- `filesystem-mcp#15` (signed receipts) was answered: no signing keys in the server, but populated `artifacts[].sha256` digests for produced files are a change worth taking.

## [1.9.24] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- Cytosol `3.2.6` accepts what `browser_observe` actually reports. `browser_fill_form` keys resolve in order — a ref number from the last observe/get_state, a bare name or id, then the key as a CSS selector — so the observe → fill path no longer misses and every existing selector caller keeps working. Attribute values are quoted, so a field name containing a quote cannot break out of the selector. An unmatched key now aborts the call and names what it tried instead of reaching `page.fill` and blocking for the full 30-second locator timeout; a miss resolves in milliseconds.

## [1.9.23] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- Enzyme `4.0.6` scores every search result on query-term coverage with a phrase bonus, title weighted above snippet, and drops results below a named floor. Wikipedia's floor is higher (0.4) than Google's (0.16) because its OR-matched recall is cheap and its precision is not: the scatter query that returned Smalltalk and XML now returns nothing, while a precise query still returns five pages. `research_brief` and `multi_site_search` apply cheap query-class priors, every result line carries its score, and `academic_search` enforces `dateRange` on arXiv with a submittedDate window plus a published-date post-filter — a 2021 paper can no longer answer a `y2` query.
- Nucleus `3.0.6` passes any command containing `;`, `&` or `|` to the shell instead of treating the whole string as a working directory, so `cd /tmp && echo marker-ok` runs; only a standalone `cd` updates the session directory, and it takes its first path argument so a trailing option is not swallowed.
- Runtime `1.3.6` types the cell RPC boundary: `callTool` resolves a validated MCP tool result and raises `CellProtocolError` on a JSON-RPC error or an unexpected shape instead of forwarding `undefined`; cell directory resolution no longer consults `process.cwd()` and names the root and every path tried when a cell is missing; and a malformed JSON-RPC frame rejects its request immediately rather than costing a full timeout.

### Changed
- One agent tool: Mitosis's cell-local `agent_run` was advertised next to the runtime-native `hela.agent.run` and carried the runtime description, so callers could not tell which one ran. Only `hela.agent.run` is exposed now.
- Genome `3.0.5` adds `npm run vault:conflicts`, which archives frontmatter-only sync conflicts without rewriting the note and lists body-divergent ones for a per-note decision. First pass: 641 conflicts archived, 615 left across 302 notes.

## [1.9.22] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- The licence wording in the legal pages, `llms.txt` and the JSON-LD licence list was hand-written, so a seventh copyleft cell would have left those statements stale — the same failure mode as the old runtime prose. They are now generated from `config/inventory.json`: counts, cell names, the always-installed set, the structured-data licence URLs and the machine-readable line all follow the inventory, and meta descriptions no longer encode a count that can drift.
- A test recomputes those strings from the inventory and fails on any divergence; `docs:check` also rejects a stale page, verified by flipping one cell's licence.

## [1.9.21] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- Runtime `1.3.4` no longer hides a cell whose catalog manifest went stale: each cell's manifest source is logged with the regeneration command, only stale cells are probed once so their tools stay advertised, and the sources are exposed on `/readyz`. On servy this had silently reduced the surface from 240 to 209 tools.
- Cytosol `3.2.5` reconnects once when the browser context was closed under it; a blank page is reported instead of retried, because the previous call may already have acted.
- Plastid `3.0.5` fails honestly when a headless Blender render writes no file, instead of returning a path to nothing.
- Mitosis `3.0.8` and Membrane `3.0.5` complete the zod 4 / glob 14 migration; `npm audit --omit=dev` now reports zero vulnerabilities in every cell and the runtime.

### Added
- Genome `3.0.4` stamps `PRAGMA user_version` after creating its schema, treats a rerun as a no-op and refuses a database written by a newer build.
- `npm run nix:hash` in the runtime refreshes the flake's npm dependency hash and rebuilds to confirm, so a version bump no longer costs a CI round trip.

## [1.9.20] - 2026-11-19

### Added
- `docs/deployment-2026-11-19.md`: the servy rollout record for 1.9.19 / runtime 1.3.3 — eight-cell `dev-workspace` roster, Nix package, staged wrapper, drop-in switch, backups and rollback, plus the stale-digest failure that hid two cells until the catalog was regenerated on the host.

## [1.9.19] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- The legal pages still claimed the whole ecosystem was MIT and granted sublicensing and sale over code that is GPL-3.0-or-later. Terms (EN and ID), their meta and JSON-LD descriptions, `llms.txt` and the `SoftwareApplication` structured data now state the split: MIT repository, six GPL-3.0-or-later cells named explicitly, per-cell terms govern redistribution. A test fails if the blanket claim returns.

### Added
- Documented the runtime update tools (`hela.update.check`, `hela.update.apply`) in the README, the on-demand guide and `llms.txt`. They already shipped with runtime 1.3.x; the docs now name them so agents can find them.

## [1.9.18] - 2026-11-19

### Changed
- `npm audit fix` across nine cells and the runtime cleared a critical advisory in Mitosis and Cytosol plus twenty others: mitosis 11 to 3, cytosol 9 to 0, nucleus 8 to 0, membrane 10 to 3, genome/ribosome/enzyme/phenotype/runtime 2 to 0, receptor 1 to 0. The remaining findings need breaking majors (zod 4, glob 14) and stay with their open dependabot PRs.
- Runtime `1.3.3` refreshed its Nix fixed-output dependency hash, verified with a local `nix build` before release.
- No tool surfaces changed (292 base tools); the version guards kept every `ServerInfo` in step.

## [1.9.17] - 2026-11-19

### Added
- Per-cell licence disclosure (PR #7): `config/inventory.json` now carries each cell's licence, the library footer and page headers derive the real blend (MIT suite + six GPL-3.0-or-later cells) instead of a blanket MIT claim, and the architecture reference states which copyleft cells every profile installs. Derived from the inventory and covered by tests.

### Fixed
- `update --json` (PR #6) emits one compact document, so a caller reading the last stdout line cannot be defeated by installer output.

## [1.9.16] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed
- Runtime prose sat outside the single-sourcing pipeline: the architecture cards (EN and ID) and the on-demand guide said `1.2.1` while the inventory said `1.3.2`, and CI stayed green because the generator skipped the `hela-runtime` prose entirely. `generate-docs` now rewrites those sentences from the inventory, `docs:check` fails on drift (verified by deliberately reverting a mention), and a test covers both languages while keeping the dated Servy rollout record at the version it actually deployed.

## [1.9.15] - 2026-11-18

### Fixed
- The tmux provisioning tests inherited `CI` from `process.env`, so on GitHub Actions provisioning short-circuited to `skipped`/`ci` before any assertion: eight failures that only existed on CI. The fixtures now strip CI variables, and the CI-disable case keeps its own explicit test.

## [1.9.14] - 2026-11-18

### Fixed
- Cytosol `3.2.3`: `BROWSER_HEADLESS` defaults to auto — headless without `DISPLAY`, headful with one, explicit values still winning. Display-less service processes could not launch Chromium before. `resolveHeadless` is exported and tested.

# Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to the HeLa MCP Ecosystem

Thank you for your interest in contributing to the **HeLa MCP Ecosystem**! This document provides guidelines and information for contributors and maintainers.

![Blotcat carefully placing a new, glowing building block on top of an established, complex structure](assets/blotcat-contributing.jpg)

---

## 1. Architectural Boundaries & 10-MCP Ceiling

* **The 10-MCP Capability Ceiling**: The ecosystem maintains exactly 10 canonical MCP servers (7 core headless, 3 specialized GUI/device). Contributions focus on reliability, performance, tool quality, and testing rather than adding new server repositories.
* **The 4-Tier Naming Architecture**:
  * Tier 1: Public Identity (`HeLa <Component>`, e.g. *HeLa Mitosis*, *HeLa Genome*)
  * Tier 2: Machine Identifier (`hela-*`, e.g. `hela-mitosis`, `hela-genome`)
  * Tier 3: Technical Source Repository (`chaining-mcp`, `project-mcp`, etc.)
  * Tier 4: Immutable Commit Hash (the selected immutable snapshot in `config/snapshots/`)
* **Repository Autonomy**: Upstream repositories remain independent and modular.

---

## 2. Development & Verification Workflow

### 2.1 Local Environment Setup
```bash
git clone https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/hela-mcp-ecosystem.git
cd hela-mcp-ecosystem
node setup.mjs --profile dev-workspace --client skip --non-interactive
```

### 2.2 Running Diagnostics & Tests
Before submitting changes, ensure all test suites pass locally:

```bash
# 1. Run diagnostic health checks
npm run doctor

# 2. Run 80-combination client configuration checks
npm run test:matrix

# 3. Run standalone MCP integration (tool counts depend on features)
npm test

# 4. Keep generated versions, tool references and site metadata current
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run docs:generate
npm run docs:check
npm run test:docs

# 5. Run configured pre-commit checks
pre-commit run --all-files
```

### 2.3 Version bumps touch seven surfaces

A release is only consistent when every surface names the same version. `npm run docs:check`
ends with `scripts/check-release-consistency.mjs`, which fails with a per-surface list, so
this is enforced rather than remembered:

| Surface | What it must say |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | the version itself — the source of truth |
| `config/snapshots/v<version>.json` | exists, with matching `snapshot_version` |
| `config/snapshots/latest-stable.json` | `snapshot_version` = new version |
| `README.md` | `Current source snapshot: **v<version>**` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | leading `## [<version>] - YYYY-MM-DD` entry |
| `RELEASE_NOTES.md` | leading `## v<version>` entry |
| `docs/current-versions.md` | `Ecosystem **<version>**` |

The snapshot pair is the one people forget, and forgetting it is not cosmetic: docs then
advertise `--snapshot v<version>`, and the installer has nothing to resolve. Regenerate the
rest rather than editing by hand:

```bash
npm version <version> --no-git-tag-version
npm run catalog:generate     # only when the tool surface changed
npm run docs:generate
npm run docs:check           # includes the consistency guard
```

### 2.3 Build and preview the complete documentation site

Use Node.js 22 LTS. Markdown rendering is a pinned build-only dependency; visitors receive static HTML, not a client-side Markdown framework.

```bash
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run docs:generate
npm run docs:build
python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory _site
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/library.html`. The builder publishes tracked root documentation, all Markdown under `docs/` (except website source files), the license, and public configuration examples. Add new documents to Git before building so they enter the publication inventory. Untracked notes, credentials, databases, Git internals and unrelated directories are not published.

The document bodies remain in their source language; English and Indonesian navigation lead to the same source content. Dated verification reports are labeled historical. Relative document links, heading anchors and illustrations resolve within the website; original source downloads and `llms-full.txt` are generated from the same files.

`npm run test:docs` checks publication coverage, links and anchors, safe Markdown rendering, source downloads, search, and deterministic builds. The existing Pages workflow installs the locked dependencies, checks the docs, and publishes `_site` to `gh-pages` when public documentation changes. Do not edit `_site` by hand.

---

## 3. Pull Request Guidelines

1. **Target Branch**: Target the maintained default branch (`master`) unless a maintainer requests a release/development branch.
2. **Commit Conventions**: Follow standard Conventional Commits:
   * `feat(scope): ...`
   * `fix(scope): ...`
   * `docs(scope): ...`
   * `test(scope): ...`
   * `chore(scope): ...`
3. **CI Matrix Conformance**: Configuration checks cover `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` on Node.js 18, 20, and 22; documentation builds and tests run on Node 22. This is not MCP runtime compatibility evidence for Node 18; use Node 22 LTS for the tested full-stack development environment. Hardware, provider and authenticated GUI integrations need separate validation.

---

## 4. Attribution & Recognition

The HeLa project respectfully recognizes **Henrietta Lacks** and the enduring scientific legacy of HeLa cells as an inspiration for immortal, modular cellular architecture in software.


---

# Source: README.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/README.html

# HeLa MCP Ecosystem

A modular, immortal cellular AI tooling ecosystem built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), engineered by Azzar to equip AI agents with full-spectrum autonomous capabilities across reasoning, persistent memory, workspace management, system execution, research, design, device automation, and 3D modeling.

> **New to MCP?** Read the **[Beginner's Guide](docs/beginner-guide.md)** for requirements, profile selection, installation, and verification.

**Read all documentation on the website:** [Document library](https://hela.my.id/library.html) · [Navigasi Bahasa Indonesia](https://hela.my.id/id/library.html). Guides, release history, contribution rules, and verification reports are published in full, with search and source downloads. Documents retain their source language.

Current source snapshot: **v1.11.26**, with runtime **1.4.5**. True first-call startup, fingerprinted discovery caches, canonical inventory tooling, profile-aware local capabilities, and managed snapshot updates are implemented; see [on-demand runtime](docs/on-demand-runtime.md) and [installation updates](docs/installation.md#updates-and-automatic-checks). Authenticated Zed/Codex ACP sessions, hardware integrations, and live vault conflict resolution remain separate; see [release notes](RELEASE_NOTES.md).

![Blotcat plugging MCP server cables into the central AI Hub](assets/blotcat-hero.jpg)

---

## Respectful Attribution & Metaphor

The **HeLa MCP Ecosystem** is named in respectful recognition of **Henrietta Lacks** (1920–1951) and the immortal scientific legacy of HeLa cells, which transformed global biomedical research. In this software architecture, HeLa serves as a **cellular biology metaphor**:

* **Cellular Modularity**: Just as biological cells contain specialized organelles coordinated by the nucleus and genome, the HeLa MCP Ecosystem deploys specialized tool servers coordinated by a dual backbone.
* **Continuous Replicability & Immortality**: Environments can be snapshot-pinned, reproduced deterministically on any machine, and restored cleanly without state degradation.
* **Component Independence**: Underlying repositories, technical package names, and Git commit histories remain autonomous and unaltered while functioning as a harmonious organism.

---

## Dual-Backbone Architecture

Every profile in the HeLa ecosystem is anchored by two core backbone servers:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Agent["Agent / LLM Orchestrator"]

    Mitosis["HeLa Mitosis<br/>(Orchestrator)<br/>- Dynamic Routing<br/>- Step Reasoning<br/>- Tool Planning"]
    Genome["HeLa Genome<br/>(State & Memory)<br/>- Knowledge Graph<br/>- Entities / Relations<br/>- Observations"]

    Membrane["HeLa Membrane<br/>Workspace FS"]
    Nucleus["HeLa Nucleus<br/>Command Exec"]
    Ribosome["HeLa Ribosome<br/>PTY Harness"]
    Enzyme["HeLa Enzyme<br/>Research / Wiki"]
    Cytosol["HeLa Cytosol<br/>Browser + Vision"]

    Agent -- "stdio JSON-RPC" --> Mitosis
    Agent -- "stdio JSON-RPC" --> Genome
    Mitosis <-->|"Shared Context"| Genome
    Mitosis --> Membrane & Nucleus & Ribosome & Enzyme & Cytosol
    Genome --> Membrane & Nucleus & Ribosome & Enzyme & Cytosol
```

* **HeLa Mitosis (`hela-mitosis`)**: Cellular division and orchestration backbone. Handles dynamic tool routing, prompt decomposition, Needle-backed sequential reasoning (`sequentialthinking` / `agent_run`), and multi-tool planning.
* **HeLa Genome (`hela-genome`)**: Cellular memory and state backbone. Maintains the persistent SQLite knowledge graph (`memory.db`), entity-relation tracking, session restoration, and project milestones.

---

## 10-MCP Component Taxonomy

| Canonical Identity | Machine ID (`id`) | Technical Source Repo | Scope | Cellular Metaphor & Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **HeLa Mitosis** | `hela-mitosis` | [`chaining-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/chaining-mcp) | Core | **Orchestrator**: Bundled Needle 3 agent runtime, dynamic routing, 40 bundled prompt templates |
| **HeLa Genome** | `hela-genome` | [`project-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/project-mcp) | Core | **State Backbone**: Entity-relation knowledge graph, milestone tracking, memory persistence |
| **HeLa Membrane** | `hela-membrane` | [`filesystem-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/filesystem-mcp) | Core | **Workspace**: Sandboxed filesystem operations, recursive search, archive extraction |
| **HeLa Nucleus** | `hela-nucleus` | [`terminal-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/terminal-mcp) | Core | **Execution**: Command execution, subshell isolation, RTK token-optimized execution |
| **HeLa Ribosome** | `hela-ribosome` | [`menager-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/menager-mcp) | Core | **Process Harness**: Interactive PTY multiplexing, Regex hooks, lifecycle management |
| **HeLa Enzyme** | `hela-enzyme` | [`researcher-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/researcher-mcp) | Core | **Knowledge**: Zero-key dual-tier web search + arXiv + Google News RSS + Wikipedia synthesis and fact-checking |
| **HeLa Cytosol** | `hela-cytosol` | [`browser-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/browser-mcp) | Core | **Interaction & vision**: Playwright automation, accessibility/DOM perception, OCR, visual analysis, detection, segmentation, and standalone image analysis |
| **HeLa Phenotype** | `hela-phenotype` | [`designer-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/designer-mcp) | Specialized | **Design**: UI/UX design tokens, OKLCH color palettes, Tailwind and component synthesis |
| **HeLa Receptor** | `hela-receptor` | [`scrcpy-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/scrcpy-mcp) | Specialized | **Mobile**: Android device automation, ADB bridge, XML view hierarchy inspection |
| **HeLa Plastid** | `hela-plastid` | [`ll3m-mcp`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/ll3m-mcp) | Specialized | **3D Modeling**: Autonomous Blender procedural modeling, materials, and render pipeline |

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Prerequisites
* **Node.js**: use Node 22 LTS for the tested full stack. Individual packages declare their own engine ranges; Receptor requires 22 and Enzyme requires at least 20.18.1.
* **Git**: `>= 2.30.0`
* **SQLite**: Genome uses Node bindings; the SQLite CLI is optional for inspection.

### 🤖 Install via AI Agent (One-Click Copy)

If you are using an AI coding assistant (Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Antigravity, Windsurf), you can copy and paste this autonomous prompt directly into your agent's chat:

```text
Please autonomously install and configure the HeLa Cellular MCP Ecosystem through one profile-aware hela-runtime MCP endpoint:

1. Environment & Harness Detection:
   Verify Node.js (>= 22.x LTS), Git (>= 2.30.0), and build tools. Identify current client (Cursor, Claude, OpenCode, Antigravity, Zed, Codex).

2. Confirm the profile with the user before installing:
   Show https://hela.my.id/profiles.html for the quick comparison, and https://hela.my.id/library/docs/profiles.html for detailed persona, workflow, server membership, and prerequisite explanations. Ask which profile best fits the user's work: minimal, dev-workspace, headless-server, research, web-devops, android-testing, 3d-modeling, or all.
   Wait for the user's choice and call it <confirmed_profile>. If they do not choose, use minimal. Do not run setup until the profile is confirmed.

3. Clone & Install the Managed Runtime:
   git clone https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/hela-mcp-ecosystem.git
   cd hela-mcp-ecosystem
   # Windows PowerShell: .\setup.ps1 ... and .\setup.ps1 doctor ...
   # macOS/Linux: node setup.mjs ... (setup.sh remains a compatibility shim)
   node setup.mjs --profile <confirmed_profile> --client <detected_client> --mode runtime --non-interactive
   node setup.mjs doctor --profile <confirmed_profile> --mode runtime
   Safely merge generated client configuration into my active MCP configuration file.
   Do not deploy or configure each hela-* cell as a separate client server.

4. Synchronize Companion Skills:
   Run `npm run skills:sync -- --profile <confirmed_profile>` from the ecosystem checkout. This reads the manifest from `config/inventory.json` and mirrors the selected organelles' bundled skills into the harness skill directory.

5. Load the Runtime Profile Context:
   - If the selected workspace has no `agent_persona/` and no existing `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `GEMINI.md`, the installer creates the profile-aware HeLa persona there and links the harness entrypoints to it.
   - If a persona already exists, preserve it; do not overwrite the user's instructions. The runtime profile context remains authoritative for active organelles and tools.
   - The generated HeLa persona is a distributable synthesis of Azzar's private Frea and Mema personal AI assistant personas: Frea contributes autonomous technical execution, while Mema contributes security and continuity discipline. Their private files, memories, credentials, and identifiers are not copied.
   - After connecting, read the `hela://profile/context` resource or request the `hela-profile-bootstrap` MCP prompt.
   - Treat the selected runtime profile as the authority for active organelles and available tools.

6. Final Handshake:
   Initialize the workspace memory graph through the exposed Genome tool when that organelle is active, and confirm the selected profile and runtime tools.
```

### 2. Run Diagnostics (`node setup.mjs doctor`)
Clone the source, then select an installation mode:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/hela-mcp-ecosystem.git
cd hela-mcp-ecosystem
node setup.mjs --mode runtime --profile dev-workspace --client opencode --non-interactive
node setup.mjs doctor --mode runtime --profile dev-workspace
```

### 3. Interactive Installation & Profile Selection
```bash
node setup.mjs
```

### 4. Non-Interactive One-Liners

**Full Developer Desktop (Cursor IDE):**
```bash
node setup.mjs --profile dev-workspace --client cursor --non-interactive
```

**Headless Linux Server (Claude Desktop / CLI):**
```bash
node setup.mjs --profile headless-server --client claude --non-interactive
```

**Pinned Immutable Release Snapshot:**
```bash
node setup.mjs --profile dev-workspace --client cursor --snapshot v1.11.26 --non-interactive
```

**Single-endpoint Runtime (one MCP connection for the selected profile):**
```bash
node setup.mjs --profile dev-workspace --client opencode --runtime --non-interactive
```

**Change an existing installation's mode in place:**
```bash
node setup.mjs mode --prefix /path/to/prefix --mode docker-runtime --client opencode --non-interactive
```

**Docker cells, Docker runtime, or Nix runtime:**
```bash
node setup.mjs --mode docker --profile dev-workspace --client cursor --non-interactive
node setup.mjs --mode docker-runtime --profile dev-workspace --client opencode --non-interactive
node setup.mjs --mode nix --profile dev-workspace --client codex --non-interactive
```

Installs use private managed prefixes under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/hela/installations/`. Existing repositories and live client files are not overwritten. Review and merge the generated client fragment. Use `--prefix` for an explicit location and pass it to doctor. See [installation modes and doctor](docs/installation.md) for HTTP transport, Compose, Nix GC roots, snapshots, optional model assets, prerequisites, and failure recovery.

---

## Supported AI Clients & Output Formats

The installer writes private fragments inside its prefix, never directly into live client files:

- Cursor, Claude, Gemini, Antigravity: `mcpServers` JSON.
- OpenCode and Kilo: `mcp` JSON with an installed local launcher, or a runtime HTTP URL.
- Zed: `context_servers` JSON; preserve unrelated settings when merging.
- Codex: `[mcp_servers.*]` TOML, with a launcher or HTTP URL.
- Docker: functional `compose.json` for the built image, not speculative per-cell Dockerfiles or stdio port mappings.

`--client skip` installs without generating a client fragment. Client authentication and GUI acceptance remain separate.

---

## Available Agent Profiles

| Profile ID | Target System | Backbone Included | Servers Included | Focus Area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minimal` | Any | Mitosis + Genome | Enzyme | Research and memory without GUI dependencies |
| `dev-workspace` | Any (GUI recommended) | Mitosis + Genome | Membrane, Nucleus, Ribosome, Enzyme, Phenotype, Cytosol | Full-stack software engineering, testing, web UI |
| `headless-server` | Headless Linux | Mitosis + Genome | Membrane, Nucleus, Ribosome, Enzyme, Phenotype | Cloud server administration, CI/CD, headless dev |
| `research` | Headless or GUI | Mitosis + Genome | Enzyme, Membrane, Cytosol | Deep literature research, document synthesis, web crawling |
| `web-devops` | Headless or GUI | Mitosis + Genome | Membrane, Nucleus, Phenotype, Cytosol | Frontend development, Tailwind styling, DOM verification |
| `android-testing` | Device connected | Mitosis + Genome | Nucleus, Receptor, Enzyme | Mobile QA testing, ADB automation, APK validation |
| `3d-modeling` | GUI (Blender installed) | Mitosis + Genome | Plastid, Membrane, Nucleus | 3D procedural modeling, materials, rendering |
| `all` | Full workstation | Mitosis + Genome | All 10 HeLa MCP servers | Complete full-spectrum AI agent capabilities |

> **Single-endpoint serve mode:** add `--runtime` to a profile command. If no profile is selected, the runtime and installer default to `minimal`; choose `dev-workspace` or another profile explicitly.

Profiles are installation choices, not machine-specific code paths. All eight pass isolated runtime verification with namespacing off/on (**16 checks**), including exact tool/schema parity and safe read-only routing. Lappy's ten-server `all` roster and servy's eight-cell `dev-workspace` setup remain different by design. See [all-profile verification](docs/profile-verification-2026-11-06.md); run `npm run test:profiles`, or append `-- --profile <id>` on a partial installation.

Runtime discovery now starts **zero cells**; only invoked cells are started. [Generated profile counts](docs/generated-profile-counts.md) come from the inventory/catalog rather than static client-specific totals. `node setup.mjs doctor --profile <id> --runtime` checks cold catalog parity as well as versions, paths, and revisions.

For complete persona guides and pipeline specifications, see **[Profiles Catalog](docs/profiles.md)**.

---

## Operational Workflows (Workflows A–F)

The ecosystem is built for structured multi-server agent workflows:
* **Workflow A: Autonomous Feature Engineering**: Genome (restore) → Mitosis (decompose) → Membrane (code) → Nucleus (test) → Genome (persist).
* **Workflow B: Deep Research & Architecture Synthesis**: Enzyme (search) → Cytosol (scrape) → Mitosis (synthesize) → Genome (record) → Membrane (write).
* **Workflow C: Web Feature with Design & Browser Verification**: Phenotype (tokens) → Membrane (build) → Nucleus (serve) → Cytosol (DOM QA) → Genome (record).
* **Workflow D: Mobile App Test Automation**: Genome (issue) → Nucleus (adb) → Receptor (drive UI) → Genome (record pass).
* **Workflow E: Autonomous 3D Asset Creation & Render Pipeline**: Genome (spec) → Mitosis (plan) → Plastid (Blender) → Membrane (save) → Genome (record).
* **Workflow F: Long-Horizon Complex Refactor with PTY Harness**: Ribosome (PTY) → Nucleus (exec) → Genome (persist).

For step-by-step tool invocation sequences, schemas, and diagrams, see **[Workflows & Integration Guide](docs/workflows.md)**.

## Project Health & Diagnostics

```bash
# Run system and server diagnostic health check
npm run doctor
# or
node setup.mjs doctor

# Run 80-combination client configuration checks (not GUI integration)
npm run test:matrix
npm run build:all -- --profile <confirmed_profile>
npm run test:all -- --profile <confirmed_profile>

# Run master integration test suite across all 10 servers (tool counts are feature-dependent)
npm test

# Sync bundled agent skills into the harness skills directory
npm run skills:sync

# Report skill drift without changing the target
npm run skills:check
```

## Updating

Check for a newer snapshot without changing anything, then apply it behind an explicit confirmation:

```sh
node setup.mjs update check --prefix <installation>
node setup.mjs update apply --confirm --prefix <installation>
```

Agents get the same controller through the runtime endpoint: `hela.update.check` (read-only, reports the snapshot delta) and `hela.update.apply` (confirmation-gated, stages through the pinned installer, verifies with doctor, and records a rollback directory). A successful apply returns `restartRequired: true`; restart the runtime or client to load the new build.

This repository — the installer, runtime glue, configuration, and documentation — is distributed under the MIT License.

The cells it installs are separate upstream projects under their own licences, and six of the ten are copyleft:

| Licence | Cells |
| --- | --- |
| GPL-3.0-or-later | Mitosis (`chaining-mcp`), Genome (`project-mcp`), Membrane (`filesystem-mcp`), Ribosome (`menager-mcp`), Enzyme (`researcher-mcp`), Plastid (`ll3m-mcp`) |
| MIT | Nucleus (`terminal-mcp`), Cytosol (`browser-mcp`), Phenotype (`designer-mcp`), Receptor (`scrcpy-mcp`), Runtime (`hela-runtime`) |

Mitosis and Genome are members of every profile, so **every install — `minimal` included — places GPL-3.0-or-later code on disk.** Weigh that against your own licence policy before deploying. Per-cell licences are listed in [current versions](docs/current-versions.md) and on each card in the architecture reference; `config/inventory.json` is the source both are generated from.

Underlying repositories remain independently copyrighted by their respective authors.

The HeLa project respectfully recognizes **Henrietta Lacks** and the enduring scientific legacy of HeLa cells.
