# Source: docs/reliability.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/docs/reliability.html

# HeLa MCP Reliability Contract

How the MCP stack is wired, what breaks it, and how to repair it. Written after the
2026-11-20 outage where `apt-get autoremove` purged `nodejs` and every MCP host
failed with `NotFound: ChildProcess.spawn (/usr/bin/node …)`.

Audited 2026-11-21 by a second agent against the live system; every number here was
re-measured or dropped. Where a figure is approximate, it says so.

## How the diagrams work

Each diagram exists twice, on purpose:

- **Rendered SVG** in `assets/diagrams/*.svg`, embedded below. This is what `markm`
  displays — its renderer is `markdown-it` + `highlight.js` + `katex` with **no Mermaid
  plugin**, so a raw Mermaid block would appear as code. It also runs with `html: false`
  and escapes raw HTML, which is why this document contains no `<details>` or inline
  `<img>` tags: they would print as literal text.
- **Mermaid source** in `assets/diagrams/*.mmd`, linked under each diagram. Edit there and
  re-render; never hand-edit an SVG.

Relative image paths are safe: markm rewrites a relative image reference into
`data-local-src`, resolves it against the open document's directory (normalising `..`),
then loads it through Neutralino's `filesystem.readBinaryFile`.

GitHub, Obsidian and VS Code render the embedded SVG natively.

Regenerate after editing any `.mmd`:

```bash
cd assets/diagrams
for f in *.mmd; do
  PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome \
    npx -y @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli@11 -i "$f" -o "${f%.mmd}.svg" -b white -t neutral
done
# mermaid-cli writes no trailing newline; the pre-commit end-of-file hook rejects that.
for f in *.svg; do [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$f")" ] && printf '\n' >> "$f"; done
```

White background with the `neutral` theme on purpose: the SVGs stay readable in light
and dark viewers alike.

| Diagram | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| 1. Layer map | What talks to what, and who owns which failure? |
| 2. Boot timeline | What happens between "host starts" and "305 tools"? |
| 3. Triage tree | Host says *failed* — where do I look first? |
| 4. Cell supervision | Why did one tool stop working mid-session? |
| 5. Trust boundaries | Who can write credentials, and what can the sandbox touch? |
| 6. Incident anatomy | How did the 11-20 outage actually unfold? |
| 7. Check loop | What runs hourly, and what may it change on its own? |
| 8. Before/after | Why is it one launcher instead of six inline configs? |

**Naming:** there are **5 client applications** and **6 config files** — Gemini keeps two
(`~/.gemini/settings.json` and `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`). Diagrams that say
"configs" mean six; diagrams that name hosts show five.

---

## 1. Layer map

![Layer map](../assets/diagrams/01-layer-map.svg)

*Source: [01-layer-map.mmd](../assets/diagrams/01-layer-map.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

- The **host** only knows one command. If it reports failure, the problem is at or below
  the launcher — never "that one client's settings" unless `hela-doctor` says `hosts` is
  drifting.
- The **cells** are children of the runtime. If the runtime boots and lists tools, the
  host is healthy even if one cell later dies (diagram 4).
- The launcher's own overhead is ~6 ms. A bare `node` start is ~25 ms, so the launcher is
  not a meaningful cost — it is one shell process plus four tests the runtime would
  otherwise fail on later with a worse message.

### Why the shape changed

![Before and after](../assets/diagrams/08-before-after.svg)

*Source: [08-before-after.mmd](../assets/diagrams/08-before-after.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

The left side is what the machine looked like before this work: five clients each holding
27–31 env vars inline, two of them already disagreeing on `NEEDLE_TOOL_INDEX_PATH` and
`HELA_ALLOWED_ROOTS`, and every one of them pinning `/usr/bin/node`. The right side is
today: identical command everywhere, one file to rotate, one place to repair.

## 2. Boot timeline

![Boot timeline](../assets/diagrams/02-boot-timeline.svg)

*Source: [02-boot-timeline.mmd](../assets/diagrams/02-boot-timeline.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

Measured three times against the launcher: `initialize` is answered at ~257–269 ms
(mean ~262 ms), and `tools/list` adds ~3 ms. So **tool registration is the cheapest step**,
not the expensive one — nearly all of the time is Node starting and the runtime reading
its cell catalog. Budget ~300 ms total.

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `78` | unreadable secrets, missing entry, or node below the required floor |
| `127` | no node on PATH, **or** `node -v` unparseable (the message names the binary and the raw output) |
| silent | runtime booted but exposed 0 tools → `HELA_PROFILE` or manifest |

Host-side startup timeouts are separate: Codex uses `startup_timeout_sec = 60`, and the
doctor's own probe allows 90 s by default (120 s in the timer). Nothing in the chain
assumes 60 s.

Why the launcher logs to a file as well as stderr: hosts swallow child stderr. After a
failure the UI keeps only a one-line status; the log keeps the reason. The timestamp is
best-effort — if `date` is unavailable the line still records the reason, with
`unknown-time` in place of the clock.

## 3. Triage tree

![Triage tree](../assets/diagrams/03-triage.svg)

*Source: [03-triage.mmd](../assets/diagrams/03-triage.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

Start at the symptom the host actually showed. Note the asymmetry: interpreter and wiring
failures are fatal for every host, cell deaths are contained to one tool family, and
sandbox denials are normal behavior that merely reports badly.

## 4. Cell supervision

![Cell supervision](../assets/diagrams/04-supervision.svg)

*Source: [04-supervision.mmd](../assets/diagrams/04-supervision.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

Restart delays are **1 s, 2 s, 4 s**. The code caps the delay at 8 s, but with the default
three attempts that cap is unreachable — the third failure marks the cell dead before any
delay is computed.

More important, and easy to misread: **the attempt counter is never reset**. A cell that
crashes, recovers, crashes, recovers, then crashes again is dead on that third crash, even
across hours. It is three strikes per runtime lifetime, not per outage. Only a host
restart re-arms.

## 5. Trust boundaries

![Trust boundaries](../assets/diagrams/05-trust-boundaries.svg)

*Source: [05-trust-boundaries.mmd](../assets/diagrams/05-trust-boundaries.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

Two separate boundaries, often confused: *who may write credentials* and *what the sandbox
may touch*.

`mcp.env` is **sourced as shell**, not parsed. `set -a; . "$SECRETS"` means any command
substitution or function definition in that file executes as you at every MCP session
start, across all six configs. The boundary that matters is therefore **write** access to
`~/.config/hela/` — 0700 dir, 0600 file. The launcher warns if the file is group/world
readable; `hela-doctor` fails it and `--repair` fixes it.

The `~/gdrive` exclusion is not incidental — that tree contains a Drive shortcut cycle
(a shortcut pointing back into its own folder), which makes any local traversal descend
until `PATH_MAX`. Keeping it outside the roots means the filesystem cell cannot be walked
into that trap.

## 6. Incident anatomy

![Incident timeline](../assets/diagrams/06-incident.svg)

*Source: [06-incident.mmd](../assets/diagrams/06-incident.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

The 50-minute gap between cause and symptom is the reason the launcher now logs and the
timer checks hourly. The other lesson: **restarting the app alone does not clear this** —
the host caches the failed connect, so the binary has to exist first.

## 7. Check loop

![Doctor loop](../assets/diagrams/07-doctor-loop.svg)

*Source: [07-doctor-loop.mmd](../assets/diagrams/07-doctor-loop.mmd) — edit, then re-render (see top).*

The doctor has ~22 distinct check names; which ones emit depends on state. A healthy run
today prints 17 lines (15 ok, 2 warn) in ~0.4 s including the live handshake. The two
steady-state warnings are housekeeping: credential-bearing backups, and shadowed tools.

| Layer | Check line | Detects | `--repair` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interpreter | `node`, `node-mark`, `node-floor`, `node-path`, `node-shadow`, `npm` | missing/old node, **auto-marked nodejs**, stale launcher gate, PATH shadowing | node only |
| Runtime | `manifest`, `runtime-entry`, `runtime-deps` | missing/unreadable manifest, missing `dist/index.js`, missing MCP SDK | no |
| Cells | `cells` | unbuilt entry, absent `node_modules` | no |
| Assets | `needle-engine`, `needle-model`, `needle-profile`, `scrcpy-server` | truncated model, non-executable engine, missing adb payload | no |
| Secrets | `env-file`, `env-dir`, `env-keys`, `env-credentials` | perms, missing keys, **blank/truncated credentials** | perms |
| Wiring | `hosts`, `host-mode:<name>`, `host-missing`, `host-binaries` | drift off the launcher, disabled client, dead third-party commands | no |
| Exposure | `host-secrets`, `backups`, `backups-large` | plaintext keys in configs, credential backups, unscannable large backups | chmod 600 |
| End-to-end | `live` | handshake, tool count, shadowed tools | no |

`--repair` performs four mutations, all idempotent: `apt-get install nodejs` +
`apt-mark manual`, `chmod 600` on `mcp.env`, `chmod 700` on `~/.config/hela`, and
`chmod 600` on credential-bearing `*.bak*` (including large ones it cannot scan). It never
edits a host config.

## The three failure classes seen so far

| Class | Symptom | Detection | Repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interpreter loss/downgrade | `ChildProcess.spawn (/usr/bin/node)` NotFound; or cells failing on `engines.node` | `node`, `node-mark` | `--repair` reinstalls the pinned package and re-marks it manual |
| Config drift | one client works, another doesn't; keys missing or stale | `hosts`, `env-keys` | point `command` at the launcher; restore keys from `*.bak-secrets-centralized` |
| Credential sprawl | plaintext keys in host configs or backups | `host-secrets`, `backups` | strip env blocks; chmod 600 or delete backups |

## Commands

The host layer is implemented once, in `scripts/host-layer.mjs`, reached through
`doctor.mjs --hosts`. `~/.local/bin/hela-doctor` is a thin wrapper that resolves the
checkout, so there is no second implementation to drift.

```bash
node scripts/doctor.mjs --hosts          # host layer, full check + live handshake
node scripts/doctor.mjs --hosts --json   # machine-readable
node scripts/doctor.mjs --hosts --repair # node, credential modes, backup exposure
hela-doctor --no-live                    # same, via the installed wrapper
```

The client entry point is `scripts/host-entry.sh`, installed as
`~/.local/bin/hela-runtime-mcp`. It resolves the interpreter, gates the version,
sources the credentials file and logs failures — that is the one command every host
calls.

Exit codes: `0` healthy (warnings allowed), `1` failures, `2` doctor itself broke
(`--notify` fires on 2 as well). Logs: `journalctl --user -u hela-doctor.service`;
launcher failures append to `~/.local/state/hela/logs/mcp-launcher.log` (rotated at
512 KB).

Note that a plain run is not read-only: it writes `~/.local/state/hela/node-min-major`
(the launcher's version gate) and refreshes `node-pin` (the version `--repair` restores).

## Automation

`hela-doctor.service` runs
`%h/.local/bin/hela-doctor --repair --notify --timeout 120` 2 minutes after login and
hourly thereafter. It exits 1 on genuine failures; `SuccessExitStatus=0 1` keeps that an
alert rather than a failed unit.

Two facts worth knowing:

- `Persistent=true` in the timer is inert — it only applies to `OnCalendar=` timers.
- The steady state is `0 warn` now that the credential-bearing backups are gone. The
  remaining warnings, when they appear, are housekeeping (world-readable backups,
  shadowed tools) rather than failures.

## Operating rules

1. **Never pin an absolute interpreter in host configs.** Use the launcher; it resolves
   `node` at spawn time and fails with an actionable message. Note the exception: the
   installer manifest `.hela-install.json` still carries `"node": "/usr/bin/node"`. No
   runtime code reads it — only the ecosystem's install/launch scripts and this doctor —
   so it is a latent trap, not a live one. Retire it when convenient.
2. **One credentials file, and treat it as code.** `~/.config/hela/mcp.env`, 0600, dir
   0700. It is sourced, so anyone who can write it can run code as you at every session
   start. Never paste keys into client configs; the durable copy lives in mema-vault.
3. **Keep nodejs marked manual.** `hela-doctor` now fails with `node-mark` if the mark
   drifts back to `auto` — that mark is what let `autoremove` delete the runtime the first
   time — and `--repair` re-asserts it.
4. **`HELA_ALLOWED_ROOTS` is the sandbox boundary.** Currently project, Documents,
   Downloads, persona, skills, memory, HeLa state/install, `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`. Add a root
   when a legitimate tool is denied; never restore `/`.
5. **After changing `mcp.env` or the launcher, restart the host.** A running MCP server
   keeps the env it booted with, and hosts cache a failed connect until restart.
6. **Do not pass `HELA_SECRETS_FILE` or `HELA_RUNTIME_ENTRY` through a host.** The
   launcher ignores them by design; if you find a config setting one, that is drift.

## Known limits

- **The live probe proves less than it looks.** It spawns no cell and calls no tool:
  `tools/list` is answered from the manifest cache because cells are created on first
  tool call. `[OK] live 305 tools` means node runs, the launcher gates pass, the manifest
  parses and the SDK answers. No cell is known to be executable.
- **305 of 591 declared tools are reachable.** With `HELA_NAMESPACE_TOOLS=0`, bare names
  collide across cells and the runtime keeps whichever cell registered last; the agent
  catalog resolves the same collisions first-cell-first. The doctor reports the 286
  shadowed names as a warning. Turning namespacing on exposes all of them but renames
  every tool, so it is a deliberate choice, not a flip.
- Policy denials from `filesystem-mcp` surface as `Invalid tools/call result:
  invalid_union` instead of `path escapes configured workspace roots` — the cell returns
  a malformed error shape. Access is still denied; only the message is wrong.
- `node-shadow` and `npm` warnings are informational; `--repair` cannot fix a PATH that
  resolves a different node, only the installed package.
- Diagram SVGs carry mermaid's `<foreignObject>` labels, which browsers render but
  non-browser rasterizers (librsvg, ImageMagick) drop — boxes appear empty. Use Chrome
  headless to flatten to PNG.
- Audit tooling caveat: `rtk`-wrapped `cat`/`sed`/`wc` has served a stale revision of this
  file (410 lines) while `/usr/bin/*` showed the current one. When verifying a document,
  read it with absolute binaries.

## Rollback and credential recovery

The credential-bearing backups were removed after every secret they held was copied into
**mema-vault** (Fernet, master key required):

| Vault entry | Contents |
|---|---|
| `hela-openrouter-api-key` | current provider key used by the runtime |
| `hela-github-token` | current `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| `hela-google-api-key` | current enzyme search key |
| `hela-google-cse-id` | current search engine identifier |
| `hela-*-old-20261118` (×4) | rotated values found in the deleted backups |
| `chatgpt-codex-resume-token` | conversation-resume JWT from a Codex state backup |

To rebuild `mcp.env` after a loss:

```bash
cd ~/.config/opencode/skills/mema-vault
python3 scripts/vault.py env hela-openrouter-api-key --env OPENROUTER_API_KEY --   python3 - <<'EOF'
# write the four values into ~/.config/hela/mcp.env, then chmod 600
EOF
```

Then `chmod 600 ~/.config/hela/mcp.env` and run the host doctor. Non-secret settings
(`HELA_PROFILE`, paths, cache sizes) are documented above and in the launcher itself.

Config-shaped rollbacks from before the launcher migration no longer exist on disk; the
shape they encoded is the one this document describes.


---

# Source: docs/security-audit.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/docs/security-audit.html

# Security status and verification scope

![Blotcat placing an API key into a local vault while untrusted inputs stay outside](../assets/blotcat-security-v2.png)

This is an operational status document, **not a completed security certification**. Earlier architecture descriptions overstated guarantees about sandboxing, credential isolation, offline operation, and test coverage. A process boundary, a profile, or a passing health endpoint does not establish those guarantees.

## Explicitly deferred work

Endpoint authentication, per-client authorization, exposed-credential rotation, public-exposure review, and resource/session limits remain deferred by the operator's development decision. Deferred does not mean implemented or safe for unrestricted public use. The documentation refresh does not change access controls or rotate credentials.

Filesystem, shell, PTY, browser, model-agent, and device operations can act with the server account's privileges. Scope and deploy them accordingly. Runtime profiles select eligible cells; they are not a substitute for an authorization policy or an OS sandbox.

## What the current checks establish

- Source snapshots pin revisions. Runtime schema catalogs additionally validate versions/build digests and declared feature variants; private caches separate profiles, roots, namespace modes, revisions, builds, and declared configuration.
- Isolated tests cover runtime timeouts, process exit before restart, bounded retries, first-call startup, concurrent calls, stale-cache refusal, and shutdown. This is lifecycle/reliability evidence, not complete adversarial testing.
- Doctor checks real isolated MCP initialize/discovery, selected paths/versions/revisions, and optional runtime catalog parity. Hardware, provider, and authenticated GUI checks remain separate.
- Genome's online backups include committed WAL data and validate integrity; restore refuses existing destinations and sidecars. This does not authorize overwriting an active database.
- Vault synchronization preserves divergent notes in conflict archives. Archived conflicts still need deliberate review; transport success does not prove reconciliation.

See [runtime verification](on-demand-runtime.md), [profile verification](profile-verification-2026-11-06.md), and each server's current tool reference for exact scope. Do not promote historical benchmark/test totals into current security claims.

## Credentials and generated output

Doctor and schema-generation probes do not display credential values; isolated probes exclude inherited keys and live vault hooks. Generated client configuration, however, can contain credentials explicitly supplied by its user. Treat configuration files, generator stdout, backups, and issue attachments as private. Never paste a raw client configuration or process environment into a public issue.

Presence of an API key does not prove provider readiness. Keyless research can still make network requests. Needle's local execution depends on its engine/model, and some generative operations need a configured model provider. Optional remote runtime/vault deployment also changes where data is processed and stored.

## Carry-forward validation

PTY orphan handling, SSH failures/transfers, browser network boundaries, archive/symlink policies, Android hardware, Blender execution, live search fallbacks, and external design services still need their own targeted checks. Tests for some of these exist, but full coverage is not implied by ecosystem configuration or discovery checks.

Current package versions and generated counts are in [current versions](current-versions.md). Historical release notes and immutable snapshots retain their original versions and evidence; they are not current acceptance guarantees.


---

# Source: docs/troubleshooting.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/docs/troubleshooting.html

# HeLa MCP Ecosystem Troubleshooting & Diagnostic Guide

This guide provides systematic diagnostic procedures, error code explanations, and recovery workflows for the **HeLa MCP Ecosystem**.

![Blotcat wearing a hard hat, looking at a smoking server block while consulting a thick manual](../assets/blotcat-troubleshooting.jpg)

---

## 1. Fast Diagnostic Workflow: `node setup.mjs doctor`

Before manual debugging, always run the automated diagnostic health check:

```bash
node setup.mjs doctor
# or
npm run doctor
```

To run diagnostics against a specific profile:
```bash
node setup.mjs doctor --profile dev-workspace
```

To output machine-readable JSON:
```bash
node setup.mjs doctor --json
```

For managed installations, select the installed `--mode` and profile, or use an explicit prefix:

```bash
node setup.mjs doctor --prefix /path/to/prefix --json
node setup.mjs doctor --url http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp --json
```

The URL form checks an already-running HTTP endpoint, not its remote filesystem. See [installation modes](installation.md) for Docker, Nix, listener startup, and private client fragments.

### Understanding Diagnostic Output

* **`READY`**: Managed source/build/image identity and isolated MCP initialize/discovery checks passed. Runtime modes also check cold catalog parity and private HTTP discovery.
* **`DEGRADED` / server `ERROR`**: A required check failed; inspect the JSON report for its server/error. Pending installations, changed builds, missing interpreters/images, and bad MCP replies fail readiness and return nonzero.
* **Integration scope**: Discovery does not verify Playwright executables, Android/Blender bridges, provider credentials, GUI authentication, or arbitrary workspace access. Legacy unmanaged checkout diagnostics have a different report layout.

---

## 2. Common Issues & Recovery Procedures

### 2.1 Diagnostic Failure: Missing Entrypoint or Build Artifacts

**Symptom**: `[ERROR] Entrypoint file missing` or `dist/index.js not found`.

**Root Cause**: The TypeScript source code has not been compiled into JavaScript build artifacts.

**Fix**:
For a managed prefix, rerun the original setup command with the same mode/profile/prefix. Locked dependencies and selected builds are recreated and probed. Preserve dirty working-tree changes rather than resetting them. A pending marker is cleared only after successful verification.

For manually maintained sibling checkouts:
```bash
# Rebuild all 10 servers automatically
npm run build:all

# Or build a single server manually
cd <server-directory>
npm run build
```

---

### 2.2 Server Stdio JSON-RPC Hang or Crash

**Symptom**: `[ERROR] Exited early with code 1` or tool timeouts during execution.

**Root Cause**: Node module dependencies are missing, or environment variables are malformed.

**Fix**:
```bash
# Reinstall dependencies for the failing server
cd <server-directory>
npm ci
npm run build
```

Verify stdio responsiveness manually:
```bash
node <entrypoint-file>
# The process should listen on stdin without throwing an uncaught exception. Press Ctrl+C to exit.
```

---

### 2.3 Client Does Not Recognize Configured MCP Servers

**Symptom**: Cursor, Claude, Gemini, or Zed reports that tools are not available.

**Root Cause**: Configuration file was written to the wrong path, contains relative paths, or the client was not restarted.

**Fix**:
1. **Regenerate configuration with absolute paths**:
   ```bash
   node setup.mjs --reconfigure --prefix /path/to/prefix --client cursor --non-interactive
   ```
2. **Review and merge the printed private fragment into the correct client file**. Setup does not write these live files:
   * **Cursor IDE**: `cat ~/.cursor/mcp.json`
   * **Claude Desktop**: `cat ~/.claude.json`
   * **Gemini / Antigravity**: `cat ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp_config.json`
   * **OpenCode**: `cat ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
   * **Kilo CLI**: `cat ~/.config/kilo/config.json`
   * **Zed Editor**: `cat ~/.config/zed/settings.json`
   * **Codex / ChatGPT**: `cat ~/.codex/config.toml`
3. **Check reload behavior**: some clients require a restart; Zed can restart context servers immediately when settings are saved. Back up active memory/vault state before changing sync hooks. Never paste raw client configuration containing credentials into an issue or chat.

### Zed forwards a server that Codex already defines

The message `MCP server hela-… was not started, because the Codex config already defines an MCP server with this name` refers to the forwarded duplicate. It does not prove that Codex failed to start its native entry. `codex mcp list` inspects configuration, not connectivity; check MCP startup/discovery or an actual safe tool call separately.

Zed 1.27.0 forwards project context servers to external agents; native `agent.profiles.*.context_servers` controls are not a per-ACP forwarding switch. Do not remove shared top-level `context_servers` just to silence Codex warnings: native Zed and other agents may need them.

The installed codex-acp 2.5.0 supports an optional per-agent environment override:

```json
"env": { "DISABLE_MCP_CONFIG_FILTERING": "true" }
```

Place it under `agent_servers.codex-acp` only if deliberately choosing merged forwarded/native ownership. This disables adapter duplicate filtering, **not forwarding**; it can fail when future definitions disagree. Identical definitions passed isolated merge/discovery checks, but authenticated Zed ACP sessions still require verification. Keeping Codex-owned entries and leaving this toggle unset preserves native ownership, with the duplicate warning still possible.

Source references: [Zed forwarding](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/c84af5b99cbc366d675064e52b23664a015b6e35/crates/agent_servers/src/acp.rs#L44-L65), [agent settings schema](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/c84af5b99cbc366d675064e52b23664a015b6e35/crates/settings_content/src/agent.rs#L842-L904), and [adapter toggle](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp/blob/v2.5.0/src/CodexAcpClient.ts#L1620-L1623).

---

### 2.4 Pinned Snapshot Recovery & Rollback

**Symptom**: Upstream repository changes broke a server build or altered expected tool schemas.

**Root Cause**: Moving `main`/`master` branch contains unreleased or breaking changes.

**Fix**:
Restore known-good, audited release snapshot:
```bash
node setup.mjs --snapshot v1.5.1 --profile dev-workspace --non-interactive
```

---

### 2.5 SQLite Database Lock or Corruption (`HeLa Genome`)

**Symptom**: `database is locked` or `SQLite error` in `project-mcp`.

**Possible causes**: Competing writers, a long transaction, permissions, filesystem failures, or a damaged database. A lock error alone does not prove corruption or missing WAL mode.

**Fix**:
1. Identify the actual database path and owning processes. Inspect integrity read-only:
   ```bash
   sqlite3 -readonly /absolute/path/to/memory.db "PRAGMA integrity_check;"
   ```
2. Take an online, validated backup that includes committed WAL data. Do not copy only the main file while SQLite is active; no daily-backup schedule is implied by the package.
3. Restore only to a new, absent destination with no SQLite sidecars, verify integrity, and review a controlled switchover. Never overwrite an active database. Preserve divergent Obsidian notes and existing conflict archives instead of choosing a winner automatically.

---

### 2.6 External Hardware Driver Issues

#### HeLa Receptor (Android / ADB)
* **Verify ADB availability**: `adb version`
* **Verify device connectivity**: `adb devices` (ensure device is authorized with USB debugging enabled).

#### HeLa Cytosol (Browser Automation)
* **Install Playwright browsers**:
  ```bash
  npx playwright install chromium
  ```

#### HeLa Plastid (Blender 3D)
* **Verify Blender CLI in PATH**:
  ```bash
  blender --version
  ```
* If installed outside standard PATH, create a symlink:
  ```bash
  sudo ln -s /path/to/blender /usr/local/bin/blender
  ```

---

## 3. Getting Further Support

* **Run Integration Tests**: `npm test` discovers the installed cells; use `-- --profile <id>` for a selected subset. Tool counts depend on enabled features.
* **Run Matrix Tests**: `npm run test:matrix` verifies 80 profile/client configuration combinations, not GUI authentication or hardware operations.
* **File an Issue**: Open an issue at [`Hela-Ecosystem/hela-mcp-ecosystem/issues`](https://github.com/Hela-Ecosystem/hela-mcp-ecosystem/issues) with reviewed/redacted output from `node setup.mjs doctor --json` and the failed check. Do not attach private configs or environments.

---

## Codex ACP: every model fails with `model_not_found`

**Symptom.** A Codex thread in Zed refuses to answer and the ACP log (`dev: open acp logs`) shows:

```
Unhandled error during turn: {"type":"error","status":400,
 "error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",
 "message":"The 'gpt-6-luna' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.",
 "code":"model_not_found"}}
```

The same account works in `codex exec`, which is the clue: the account is fine, the adapter is stale. `codex-acp` bundles its own Codex core, and the build shipped by the Zed registry here (`0.11.1`) carries a model list older than the account, so every model it offers — including the configured one — is rejected. Nothing is wrong with the ChatGPT login, and no credentials need to be copied anywhere.

**Fix.** Replace the registry adapter with a current one and point Zed at it as a custom agent:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/zed/agent_servers/codex-acp-2.7.0
cd ~/.local/share/zed/agent_servers/codex-acp-2.7.0
npm i @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@2.7.0
```

```json
{
  "agent_servers": {
    "codex-acp": {
      "type": "custom",
      "command": "/home/USER/.local/share/zed/agent_servers/codex-acp-2.7.0/node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp/dist/index.js",
      "args": [],
      "env": {},
      "default_config_options": { "model": "gpt-6-luna", "mode": "agent-full-access" }
    }
  }
}
```

Zed applies the settings change without a restart. Keep the model in `default_config_options` aligned with `~/.codex/config.toml`; a model that the account rejects fails the turn the same way regardless of adapter version.

**Verify without the GUI.** From an ecosystem checkout:

```sh
node scripts/verify-acp.mjs          # or: npm run test:acp
```

It reads the custom entry from `~/.config/zed/settings.json`, drives the same adapter Zed does, and passes only when the agent returns text for a real prompt. Override the binary with `HELA_ACP_AGENT_BINARY` when testing a candidate build.


---

# Source: docs/workflows.md
URL: https://hela.my.id/library/docs/workflows.html

# HeLa MCP Ecosystem: Workflows & Integration Guide

![Blotcat Workflows Orchestration](../assets/blotcat-workflows.jpg)

This document defines the standard operational workflows and cross-MCP coordination patterns enabled by the **HeLa MCP Ecosystem**.

---

## 1. Architectural Foundation: Dual-Backbone Coordination

Every profile in the HeLa MCP Ecosystem is anchored by two coordinating backbone servers:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Agent["Agent / LLM Orchestrator"]

    Mitosis["HeLa Mitosis<br/>(Orchestrator)<br/>- Dynamic Routing<br/>- Step Reasoning<br/>- Tool Planning"]
    Genome["HeLa Genome<br/>(State & Memory)<br/>- Knowledge Graph<br/>- Entities / Relations<br/>- Observations"]

    Membrane["HeLa Membrane<br/>Workspace FS"]
    Nucleus["HeLa Nucleus<br/>Command Exec"]
    Ribosome["HeLa Ribosome<br/>PTY Harness"]
    Enzyme["HeLa Enzyme<br/>Research / Wiki"]
    Cytosol["HeLa Cytosol<br/>Browser + Vision"]

    Agent --> Mitosis & Genome
    Mitosis <-->|"Shared Context"| Genome
    Mitosis & Genome --> Membrane & Nucleus & Ribosome & Enzyme & Cytosol
```

- **HeLa Mitosis (`hela-mitosis`)**: Acts as the cognitive orchestrator. It decomposes complex prompts, analyzes tool performance, and runs Needle-backed `sequentialthinking` step-by-step logic (each thought is an observe → decide → execute agent step recorded in AgentState).
- **HeLa Genome (`hela-genome`)**: Acts as the immutable project memory. It stores entities, relations, observations, and session milestones in `memory.db`.

---

## 2. Canonical Workflows Catalog

### Workflow A: Autonomous Feature Engineering

**Primary Profiles**: `dev-workspace`, `headless-server`
**Components**: `hela-genome` → `hela-mitosis` → `hela-membrane` → `hela-nucleus` → `hela-genome`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome
    participant Mitosis as HeLa Mitosis
    participant Membrane as HeLa Membrane
    participant Nucleus as HeLa Nucleus

    Agent->>Genome: get_session_context / search_nodes(task)
    Genome-->>Agent: Previous architecture & constraints
    Agent->>Mitosis: analyze_with_sequential_thinking(feature_req)
    Mitosis-->>Agent: Step-by-step implementation plan
    Agent->>Membrane: read_file / write_file(source_code)
    Membrane-->>Agent: Code written to workspace
    Agent->>Nucleus: execute_command("npm test" / "pytest")
    Nucleus-->>Agent: Test run output
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="add_observations", observations=[…])
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Context Restoration**: Call `get_session_context` on `hela-genome` to retrieve active architectural decisions and dependencies.
2. **Decomposition**: Call `llm_decompose_task` or `sequentialthinking` on `hela-mitosis` to generate an execution plan.
3. **Workspace Modification**: Call `read_file` and `write_file` on `hela-membrane` to apply minimal, production-ready code changes.
4. **Validation**: Call `execute_command` on `hela-nucleus` (or `rtk` wrapper) to run automated unit tests.
5. **State Recording**: Call `memory_edit` on `hela-genome` to commit progress to the knowledge graph.

---

### Workflow B: Deep Research & Architecture Synthesis

**Primary Profiles**: `research`, `dev-workspace`
**Components**: `hela-enzyme` → `hela-cytosol` → `hela-mitosis` → `hela-genome` → `hela-membrane`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Enzyme as HeLa Enzyme
    participant Cytosol as HeLa Cytosol
    participant Mitosis as HeLa Mitosis
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome
    participant Membrane as HeLa Membrane

    Agent->>Enzyme: wikipedia_search / google_search(query)
    Enzyme-->>Agent: Structured technical summaries & citations
    Agent->>Cytosol: browser_navigate(spec_url) -> browser_get_content(format=markdown)
    Cytosol-->>Agent: Live technical documentation content
    Agent->>Mitosis: llm_summarize(extracted_data)
    Mitosis-->>Agent: Synthesized architectural comparison
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="create_entities") + memory_edit(action="add_observations")
    Agent->>Membrane: write_file("docs/architecture/spec-x.md")
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Knowledge Retrieval**: Query `wikipedia_search` or `google_search` via `hela-enzyme` for background literature and reference APIs.
2. **Live Web Extraction**: Use `browser_navigate` and `browser_get_content(format=markdown)` via `hela-cytosol` to extract documentation from official docs sites.
3. **Synthesis**: Run `llm_summarize` and `analyze_with_sequential_thinking` on `hela-mitosis` to synthesize key architectural trade-offs.
4. **Knowledge Ingestion**: Call `memory_edit` on `hela-genome` linking findings to existing system components.
5. **Artifact Generation**: Save the final report using `write_file` on `hela-membrane`.

---

### Workflow C: End-to-End Web Feature with Design & Browser Verification

**Primary Profiles**: `web-devops`, `dev-workspace`
**Components**: `hela-phenotype` → `hela-membrane` → `hela-nucleus` → `hela-cytosol` → `hela-genome`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Phenotype as HeLa Phenotype
    participant Membrane as HeLa Membrane
    participant Nucleus as HeLa Nucleus
    participant Cytosol as HeLa Cytosol
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome

    Agent->>Phenotype: design_tokens(action="theme") / design_tokens(action="tailwind")
    Phenotype-->>Agent: Design tokens & OKLCH color palette
    Agent->>Membrane: write_file("tailwind.config.js" & component files)
    Agent->>Nucleus: execute_command("npm run dev")
    Nucleus-->>Agent: Local dev server active on port 3000
    Agent->>Cytosol: browser_navigate("http://localhost:3000") -> browser_screenshot
    Cytosol-->>Agent: Rendered screenshot, accessibility tree, and Mirage visual analysis
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="add_observations", observations=["Design verified on DOM & visual snapshot"])
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Design System Token Generation**: Call `design_tokens`, `palette`, or `logo_workflow` on `hela-phenotype`.
2. **Component Implementation**: Write JSX/Tailwind files using `write_file` on `hela-membrane`.
3. **Dev Server Launch**: Launch background local web server using `execute_command` on `hela-nucleus`.
4. **Visual & Accessibility Verification**: Navigate to `http://localhost:3000` via `browser_navigate` on `hela-cytosol`, verify DOM via `browser_get_content(format=axtree)`, take a visual snapshot with `browser_screenshot`, and use `browser_visual_analyze` when the rendered image needs scene, text, object, or layout interpretation. Use `browser_image_analyze` for a standalone image that does not come from an active browser page.
5. **Milestone Recording**: Save verification screenshot path and milestone to `hela-genome`.

> **Live Production References Generated by HeLa Phenotype (`the-designer`):**
> * [Ellis UI Archive / The Collection](https://demo-designer.glassgallery.my.id/) — 24 bespoke anti-slop design systems (*Game Boy 8-bit, Top Secret Dossier, Nutrition Facts, Library Card, Gothic Tome, Swiss Archival*).

---

### Workflow D: Mobile App Test Automation & Verification

**Primary Profiles**: `android-testing`, `all`
**Components**: `hela-genome` → `hela-nucleus` → `hela-receptor` → `hela-genome`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome
    participant Nucleus as HeLa Nucleus
    participant Receptor as HeLa Receptor

    Agent->>Genome: get_session_context (device test suite)
    Agent->>Nucleus: execute_command("adb devices")
    Nucleus-->>Agent: Connected device ID detected
    Agent->>Receptor: start_session(deviceId) -> ui_dump
    Receptor-->>Agent: XML/axtree hierarchy of active mobile screen
    Agent->>Receptor: tap(element_id) / input_text("user_input")
    Receptor-->>Agent: UI transition complete
    Agent->>Receptor: screenshot("artifacts/test-pass.png")
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="add_observations", observations=["Mobile flow X verified on physical Android"])
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Device Discovery**: Call `device_list` on `hela-receptor` or `execute_command("adb devices")` on `hela-nucleus`.
2. **Session Initialization**: Call `start_session` on `hela-receptor`.
3. **UI Hierarchy Inspection**: Call `ui_dump` or `ui_find_element` to inspect Android view hierarchy token-efficiently via XML rather than screenshots.
4. **Interaction**: Execute `tap`, `input_text`, `scroll`, or `key_event` to execute test scenario.
5. **Visual Proof & Persistence**: Call `screenshot` and record test result observation in `hela-genome`.

---

### Workflow E: Autonomous 3D Asset Creation & Render Pipeline

**Primary Profiles**: `3d-modeling`, `all`
**Components**: `hela-genome` → `hela-mitosis` → `hela-plastid` → `hela-membrane` → `hela-genome`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome
    participant Mitosis as HeLa Mitosis
    participant Plastid as HeLa Plastid
    participant Membrane as HeLa Membrane

    Agent->>Genome: search_nodes("3D Assets")
    Agent->>Mitosis: generate_route_suggestions("Procedural chair generation")
    Agent->>Plastid: generate_modeling_plan("Modern lounge chair")
    Plastid-->>Agent: Phased Python Blender script
    Agent->>Plastid: execute_blender_code(script) -> render_output
    Plastid-->>Agent: High-resolution render output PNG
    Agent->>Plastid: save_blend("assets/chair.blend")
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="add_observations", observations=["Generated 3D chair asset and render"])
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Asset Requirement Analysis**: Retrieve scene requirements from `hela-genome`.
2. **Plan Synthesis**: Call `generate_modeling_plan` on `hela-plastid`.
3. **Procedural Execution**: Run `execute_blender_code` to generate geometry, apply materials, and setup lights.
4. **Render Output**: Trigger `render_output` and `get_fast_feedback` for visual QA.
5. **Persistence**: Save `.blend` file via `save_blend` and register the asset entity in `hela-genome`.

---

### Workflow F: Long-Horizon Complex Refactor with PTY Harness

**Primary Profiles**: `dev-workspace`, `headless-server`
**Components**: `hela-ribosome` → `hela-nucleus` → `hela-genome`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent
    participant Ribosome as HeLa Ribosome
    participant Nucleus as HeLa Nucleus
    participant Genome as HeLa Genome

    Agent->>Ribosome: session_spawn("long-build", "mvn clean install -T 4")
    Ribosome-->>Agent: Session spawned (ID: sess-101)
    Agent->>Ribosome: session_read("sess-101") (bounded polling)
    Ribosome-->>Agent: Streamed stdout/stderr chunk
    Agent->>Nucleus: execute_command("git status")
    Agent->>Genome: memory_edit(action="add_observations", observations=["Long refactor build verified via PTY session"])
    Agent->>Ribosome: session_close("sess-101")
```

#### Step-by-Step Tool Sequence:
1. **Interactive Session Creation**: Call `session_spawn` on `hela-ribosome` for interactive, long-running processes (compilers, debuggers, REPLs).
2. **Session Monitoring**: Read process output with `session_read` or send input with `session_write`.
3. **Session Termination**: Clean up process with `session_close`.
4. **Memory Recording**: Log completed refactor state to `hela-genome`.

---

## 3. Best Practices & Token Economy

1. **Structured Memory Over Raw History**: Always record key findings and milestones to `hela-genome` so subsequent agent turns do not need to re-read thousands of lines of raw logs.
2. **Hierarchy Inspection Over Full Screenshots**: For web (`hela-cytosol`) and mobile (`hela-receptor`), prefer accessibility trees and XML dumps for element location, reserving bitmap screenshots for final visual verification.
3. **Fail-Fast Pre-Validation**: Always verify prerequisite binary availability via `node setup.mjs doctor` before launching complex cross-MCP pipelines.
